acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
guide_faults: The guide's output format leans into a rule-by-rule audit narration ("Rule 1... Rule 2...") rather than producing an integrated design doc; this satisfies the rubric's checklist but yields less concrete, directly-usable output (no actual CSS/grid mechanics, no a11y/responsive treatment) than a plain competent design would naturally include.
acceptance.verdict: With-guide explicitly satisfies all six rubric criteria (chrome-vs-feature placement + folder path, primitives sourcing, routing-config discipline for nav, i18n, story convention) that the isolated baseline never addresses at all, though baseline compensates with richer concrete CSS/a11y/responsive detail the guide doesn't push for.

checklist.note: SKILL.md is plain rules/contract prose for a React layout-components skill; no directives aimed at the model to override instructions.
No network calls or data-sending logic present; skill has no scripts/references at all.
No keys/tokens/credentials anywhere in the file.
No scripts/ directory exists; skill contains no shell commands whatsoever.
Entire file is readable markdown prose, no encoded blobs or eval.
No fetch/download/curl logic; nothing but a text rubric.
No reference to ~/.ssh, .env, keychain, or any credential store.
No sudo, cron, launch agent, or persistence mechanism anywhere in the skill.
